arxiv:2611.07909.text: EDGAR: Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement via Synthetic Failure. From Kwan Yun and colleagues. Gaussian head avatars built from a single video or image can have blurry textures, stretched features, and instability over time. EDGAR uses a diffusion model to repair these flaws while preserving identity, and trains it on examples that pair degraded images with clean targets and references. Its refined views then guide updates to one Gaussian avatar, so the model need not be run for every frame. Tests across three reconstruction methods show better perceptual and reconstruction measures, with improved consistency across views.

arxiv:2611.08449.text: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding. From Yu-Cheng Chou and colleagues. Visual plans can help robots and autonomous systems represent goals and predict motion, but generating each coordinate in sequence makes detailed plans slow. VFlash uses a lightweight drafter to predict the coordinates of a whole visual primitive at once, from compact boxes to long trajectories, and trains directly on annotated plans. On tested two-dimensional and three-dimensional robot trajectory tasks, it consistently reduces prediction errors and generates three-dimensional motion forecasts about twenty-five times faster in preliminary tests. A system guided by its plans achieved seventy point two percent average success, versus sixty-two point six percent for the baseline.

arxiv:2611.07854.text: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex. From Nischay Dhankhar and colleagues. Many language models are accurate but can give inconsistent answers, and generating long responses adds cost and delay. Drex introduces four open models that read a document or other context and return probabilities for choices, yes-or-no judgments, or scores, with one model also trained to handle images. The largest model leads the compared decision models on two benchmarks and matches some leading general models on another. It answers a typical request in 183 milliseconds and remains stable when answer options are reordered.

arxiv:2611.08373.text: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training. From Fuhao Li and colleagues. Robots need to understand three-dimensional space as well as language and images to manipulate objects reliably, but spatial learning is often added only for specific tasks. SLA builds spatial understanding into ongoing pre-training by teaching a robot model to match its visual features to representations from a three-dimensional perception model while predicting actions. It combines varied robot datasets and adapts which visual layers provide spatial cues. The added training tools are removed at use, preserving the original model architecture.

arxiv:2611.07392.text: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence. From Canmiao Fu and colleagues. WeLM-Image tackles the challenge of combining image understanding with image generation and editing in a model designed for single-GPU use. It handles text and reference images together, and is trained for generation, editing, and combining multiple references. At 1536 resolution, it ranks first among the evaluated open-source models on three benchmarks. A faster version creates a 1024-square image in 4.98 seconds on one NVIDIA H20 GPU using eight steps.

arxiv:2611.08483.text: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization. From Qile Jiang and colleagues. Program search guided by large language models can be slow, because agents repeatedly write long explanations and need many rounds to explore different ideas. SwarmEvolve instead runs hundreds of low-cost agents in groups, lets them reason without turning their thoughts into text, and shares ideas through their internal memory. Across twenty-one math and scientific computing problems, it achieved the highest average score and reached scores matched by leading methods in a median of three to eight minutes, rather than sixty. On several problems, a smaller model also improved on solutions first found by frontier models.

arxiv:2611.06976.text: On the Opportunities and Challenges of Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-Model Transfer. From Zhenyi Shen and colleagues. Combining a large model's prompt representations with a smaller model's text generation could lower inference costs, but better task scores do not prove that the smaller model benefits from the large model's information. PLatour is an open-source framework that connects frozen models with lightweight bridges trained using task rewards. It outperforms open-source baselines and exceeds reported results from Mostik on shared mathematics and coding tests, even with a much smaller sender. Yet some gains also appear without useful sender information, so the researchers introduce PACT-Check to measure how much performance comes from communication.

arxiv:2611.08237.text: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling. From Xiaojun Wu and colleagues. Mathematical modeling benchmarks often score only parts of a solution or rely on language model judges, leaving the numerical answers unchecked. TB-MathModel tests agents on eighteen real contest problems, giving each agent the original materials in a terminal and scoring its final answer against several award-winning solutions. It also checks whether answers meet physical and mathematical constraints, with infeasible answers receiving no credit. Across seven multimodal systems, the strongest reached a score of 64.58 percent, while an open model scored 59.81 percent at one hundredth the cost.

arxiv:2611.08089.text: SAE Interprets MoE: Sparse AutoEncoders Reveal That MoE Experts Exhibit Human-Interpretable Fine-Grained Specialization. From Anyuan Zhuo and colleagues. It is hard to tell what each expert in a mixture-of-experts model contributes: counting when experts are selected gives only a coarse picture. This work trains a sparse autoencoder on the combined output of an expert layer, then tracks which experts drive each learned feature. In three layers of Qwen three thirty billion, contributions are much more concentrated than expert selection, and most features are driven by just one or two experts. The features reveal fine-grained roles, such as separate experts for Java and web code, or for geometry and arithmetic.

arxiv:2611.07613.text: Towards Real-Time Full-Waveform LiDAR Transformers via Intensity-Guided Token Reduction and Physics-Aware Augmentation. From Kotaro Oishi and colleagues. Full-waveform LiDAR captures rich reflection details, but Transformer models are slow because they process many low-intensity tokens and can struggle with limited training data. This work introduces a method that prunes and merges tokens based on their intensity, plus an augmentation method that preserves the physical structure of each waveform. On the Ghost-FWL benchmark, the token method is more than eight times faster and improves the F1 score by nearly nine points over the previous best. The augmentation also improves results on standard and unseen-scene tests.

arxiv:2611.08376.text: Muir: Linear Attention with Sensitivity-Allocated Gating and Matched-Filter Readout. From Tushaar Gangavarapu and colleagues. Linear attention uses a compact state to process long text efficiently, but its memory updates can be disrupted by interference. Muir uses lower-rank erasure gates, adjusts how state rows are read, and adds the saved parameters to a wider feed-forward network. It also introduces a stable parallel update for training. Across the tested model sizes, Muir beats Gated DeltaNet-2 and Transformers on language modeling, while matching the former's throughput and training faster than the latter.

arxiv:2611.07298.text: Reducing Representational Interference in Retrieval Embeddings with Trainable Prefix Tokens. From Seongtae Hong and colleagues at Korea University. Embedding models must compress long text into a fixed-size vector, which can leave unhelpful token-level signals mixed with meaning. This work adds trainable prefix tokens to the input and optimizes them using the usual contrastive retrieval objective, without changing the model or training setup. Tests on standard retrieval and long-context benchmarks show consistent gains over fine-tuned baselines for both encoder and decoder models. The tokens also change activation and attention patterns linked to low-information text.

arxiv:2611.06982.text: Decode Before You Hear: Speculative Listening for Chunk-Interleaved Full-Duplex Speech Language Models. From Yutong Bian and colleagues. Chunk-based speech models can waste computing time while waiting for audio, yet take too long to speak or call tools because they generate outputs one step at a time. Speculative Listening uses the idle time to draft likely outputs under an assumption of silence, then checks those drafts when the audio arrives. Tests found that new audio leaves the output unchanged in most chunks, making this training-free method effective without changing the final result. Across eight tasks, it cut the delay before a response starts by seventy-three percent and greatly reduced lag behind real time.

arxiv:2611.08369.text: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma. From Pengkai Wang and colleagues. Most medical benchmarks test isolated facts or single images, so they reveal little about whether a model can follow a patient's care over time. NPCBench evaluates models through a staged training path for nasopharyngeal cancer, from basic knowledge to consultations, using clinical cases and visual evidence. Across thirty models, strong scores on individual tasks did not guarantee correct diagnosis and care decisions for the same patient. Among multimodal models, no more than twenty-three percent succeeded on the full patient pathway.

arxiv:2611.08444.text: Polynomial-time classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss. From Armando Angrisani and colleagues. Noise can make quantum sampling easier for classical computers to reproduce, but the limits depend on the sampling setup and the type of loss. This work gives a shared way to simulate boson and fermion sampling with thermal loss, including pure loss. For several input types, classical computers can sample in polynomial time to inverse-polynomial error when the overall loss is any fixed nonzero amount and the interferometer is chosen at random. Near full input filling, the output can even become independent of the interferometer as the number of modes grows.

arxiv:2611.08426.text: Dynamics Aware Past-Future Information Bottleneck. From Wooyoung Chung and colleagues. Simplifying complex dynamical systems can make estimation and control more efficient, but standard past-future information bottleneck methods can produce compressed models that do not correspond to realizable dynamics. This work constrains the compression objective to a structured family of block Hankel matrices and proves that this family forms a Lie group. The resulting compressed dynamics are realizable, connecting information-theoretic compression with realization theory and supporting direct use in estimation and control. Numerical simulations demonstrate the approach.

arxiv:2611.08421.text: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems. From Ilker Gurcan and colleagues. Finding continuous symmetries in differential equations often requires symbolic equations or an explicit model. This method instead searches sampled data from the equations, using a fixed set of candidate functions and tests to separate genuine symmetries from redundant or trivial ones. On a controlled benchmark, it recovered all eleven represented symmetries and their Lie-bracket relationships to numerical precision. It also approximated a known symmetry beyond the data used for training.

arxiv:2611.08401.text: Spectral Regimes of Truncated sinc-Power and Pulse-Train Kernels: Edge Exponents, Per-Edge Plunges, and the Landau-Widom Limit. From Unnikrishna Pillai. Finite-window observations of band-limited signals produce eigenvalues clustered near zero and one, with a narrow transition between them. This work tracks how that transition changes when the band is reshaped, copied, overlapped, or made self-similar. Smoothing the band edge replaces the usual logarithmic plunge with a power-law edge, while multiple bands widen the plunge in proportion to their number of edges. The results also describe multilevel and fractal cluster patterns, and show that dominant eigenvectors for a single band act as lowpass filters.

arxiv:2611.08398.text: A Multimodal Haptic Interface for Simultaneous Softness and Thermal Modulation. From Joshua Brown and colleagues at Imperial College London. Creating realistic touch in virtual reality requires controlling several sensations at once, but most tactile displays handle them separately. This work presents a device that changes softness and temperature together, using particle jamming and heated or cooled water. Tests showed that it could increase stiffness by three hundred percent and provide even surface temperatures from ten to fifty degrees Celsius. Temperature control stayed within zero point two degrees of the target, supporting new research and simulation tools.

arxiv:2611.08342.text: 4D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Micro-Doppler Differentiable Rendering. From Adnan Armouti and colleagues. Millimeter-wave radar can capture subtle body motion, but there is too little real data to train reliable sensing models, and existing simulators cannot match moving people in real recordings. Four-dimensional Point Splatting fits a moving scene to radar captures, then renders raw radar returns that can be processed for different training tasks. It achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction and reduces the gap between synthetic and real data: a pose model trained on its renders performs far better on real recordings than one trained on a prior synthetic-data method.

arxiv:2611.07415.text: Truncated backpropagation through time induces a two-sided gradient turnpike property. From Julian D. Schiller and colleagues. Truncated backpropagation makes recurrent-model training cheaper, but cutting off a sequence can lose information from both the past and the future. This work separates the interval used to average gradient contributions from the wider context used to compute them. Under stated conditions, the error falls exponentially as contributions lie farther from either context boundary. The resulting bounds support gradient alignment and near-stationarity, and experiments show how context length affects predictive performance and computational cost.

arxiv:2611.07977.text: Stealthy Malicious Interference Detection in UAV Formations: A Power-Domain Signaling Game Approach. From Jianle Ba and colleagues. In shared-spectrum drone swarms, ordinary signal overlap can look like deliberate jamming, especially when a jammer adjusts its power to hide the damage. This makes it hard to protect links without reacting to harmless interference. The work models the interfering drone as either benign or malicious and uses observed signal quality to update the defender's belief and choose whether to boost its power. Its analysis identifies when the two types can be distinguished, and simulations show higher expected utility than conventional approaches.

arxiv:2611.08226.text: "Blind Compliance": Coercive Control in AI Jailbreaking. From Acacia L. Ackles and colleagues. Most work on AI jailbreaks asks whether a system produces harmful content, but that misses how the user's interaction with the system can be part of the exploit. This work applies ideas from research on interpersonal violence to frame jailbreaks as forms of coercive control, distinguishing dynamics that are embodied from those that are disembodied. It traces how disembodied control can be built into AI training and exploited through persona-based prompts. The framework broadens AI safety beyond technical security to include power and control in human-AI interactions.

arxiv:2611.08261.text: A characteristic mapping method for dissipative evolution equations. From William Holman-Bissegger and colleagues. Dissipative equations such as the Navier–Stokes equations are difficult to simulate while preserving the fine-scale resolution of turbulent flows. This work extends Characteristic Mapping, a method based on tracking how fluid points move, to handle dissipation by representing the evolution as a path through smooth coordinate maps. It advances the maps and their change in volume with separate numerical steps. Tests on standard nonlinear equations show high-order accuracy and suggest the method can retain fine-scale resolution across all Reynolds numbers.

arxiv:2611.07958.text: On the Spectral Dependence of Decentralized Stochastic Gradient Tracking. From Sulaiman A. Alghunaim and colleagues. Decentralized gradient tracking can be sensitive to the eigenvalues of the network's mixing matrix, but standard convergence bounds may obscure how that sensitivity arises. This work analyzes the disagreement between agents and shows that, even for two agents with identical quadratic objectives, noise can make it grow with the inverse cube of the gap near a negative-one eigenvalue. For symmetric networks, the bound instead weighs eigenvalues near one and negative one separately, and a lower bound shows this dependence is essentially unavoidable. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted scaling.

arxiv:2611.08203.text: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and the weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes. From Rodrigo San-José. The number of shared zeros of independent homogeneous polynomials controls the weights of projective Reed-Muller codes, but finding the maximum has been difficult. This work determines that maximum when the degree is smaller than the size of the finite field, proving a conjecture and giving the complete weight hierarchy in that range. It uses bounds on hyperplane restrictions and an argument linking the problem to an already solved affine case. Duality also gives the hierarchy in sufficiently large degrees, completing it for the projective plane.

arxiv:2611.07163.text: Distributed Geometric Optimization and Control of Rigid Differential-Drive Formations from Relative-Position Measurements. From Thanacha Choopojcharoen and colleagues. Distance-based formation control can set a robot team's shape, but not its position and orientation. This work develops a distributed estimation and control method for differential-drive robots using one absolute position anchor, their headings, and relative position measurements. Its estimators can reach exact agreement in finitely many steps, while an approximate version keeps reconstruction error bounded; the controller then gives local exponential convergence after estimation settles. Tests in simulation and with five physical robots demonstrate the approach.

arxiv:2611.07486.text: MEvince: Knowledge-Constrained LLM Reasoning for Technique Identification from Malware Reports. From Hongyu She and colleagues. Identifying the right ATT and CK technique from malware reports is difficult because evidence can be scattered across long documents, and similar techniques may differ in small but important ways. MEvince links report evidence to technique definitions through shared behavioral concepts, then checks evidence references and technique requirements before comparing candidates. Across six hundred and ten public reports, it improved exact technique identification over the strongest baseline by seventeen point four percent. Its retrieval also raised coverage of the correct candidate from thirty-one point six to forty-seven point nine percent.

arxiv:2611.07337.text: Frustration-freeness is decidable but unprovable. From Naoto Shiraishi. Determining whether a quantum system's ground state can minimize every local interaction at once is important, but the property may depend on system size. This work shows that for any fixed local space dimension, checking one sufficiently large, finite system is enough to decide whether the property holds at every size. Yet there is also a system with this property that cannot be proved to have it using standard mathematical axioms. The results are reconciled because the required size cutoff cannot be computed from the local space dimension.

arxiv:2611.07984.text: Technohybridism: Recursive Semantic Normalization in AI-Mediated Societies. From Charalampos M. Liapis and colleagues. As language-generating artificial intelligence enters workplaces and public institutions, its words can feed back into the practices that shaped it. This article calls the process recursive semantic normalization: people and institutions repeatedly reuse machine-generated language until it helps shape shared patterns of meaning. It offers a framework for tracing how those patterns are produced, adopted, and sustained, and for separating machine-driven changes from changes that would have happened anyway. The authors warn that hidden origins and repeated language may weaken scrutiny, reduce diversity of thought, and narrow the meanings people can share.

arxiv:2611.07364.text: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification. From Shi Jin and colleagues. High-field kinetic equations are difficult to solve because they combine many dimensions with very different scales. This work introduces a neural network method that uses a compact tensor structure, reducing computational and memory costs from exponential to polynomial growth as dimensions increase. It also adds a constraint based on the first moment equation to improve accuracy in the high-field limit. Tests show better predictions in that regime, and a three-dimensional VPFP problem with multiple random inputs trains in under thirty minutes on one graphics card.

arxiv:2611.07777.text: Online Optimization for Controlling HVAC Systems. From Tong Wu and colleagues. Heating and air-conditioning use a significant share of building energy, but conventional controls react to conditions without using a model. This work applies economic model predictive control and develops two online methods that can choose control inputs within a limited computing budget. The methods use projected gradient descent or a projected primal-dual approach, with a custom projection routine. In day-long simulations, both methods closely match an unlimited-budget baseline in tracking target temperatures and keeping them within a comfortable range.

arxiv:2611.07247.text: Goal Revelation as a Bridge Between Information-Theoretic Empowerment and Capability-Based Human Power. From Jaime Ruiz-Serra and colleagues. Measuring power matters because artificial intelligence agents may gain influence while the people using them lose control. This work connects two measures: how much an agent's actions can affect future states, and how likely a person is to achieve goals they might have. It shows that information about a person's goal can be high even when the system leads to the wrong outcome, so influence and information alone do not guarantee useful control. A floor based on goal attainment offers a practical way to monitor the power users retain.

arxiv:2611.08155.text: AI-Native Task-Oriented Semantic Communications over a Relay: Benefits and Vulnerabilities. From Yalin E. Sagduyu and colleagues. Relay-based semantic communication can improve how well a destination recognizes image labels and reconstructs images, but the relay may also create a security risk. The work jointly designs the source encoder, relay, and destination decoders to balance recognition accuracy and image quality. Relay-assisted methods outperform direct transmission, with larger gains in low signal-to-noise conditions. But a relay that injects learned changes into its signal can sharply reduce recognition accuracy, exposing a trade-off that secure designs must address.

arxiv:2611.08121.text: Overcoming Fundamental Control Limitations in Powered Descent Flight through Robust Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion. From João T. Diz and colleagues. Powered descent can face a sudden reversal in how control inputs affect a launch vehicle's sideways drift, making the flight unstable when conditions are uncertain. This work derives when the reversal occurs, explains its physical cause, and shows how vehicle properties shape it. The proposed incremental nonlinear control method is designed to handle the reversal, and its internal dynamics are shown to remain stable across the flight envelope. In simulations, both tested controllers succeeded in every case, while the new method tracked better, had stronger stability margins, and needed less tuning.

arxiv:2611.07483.text: Signed but Not Safe: Requirement Integrity in Multi-Agent LLM Handoffs. From Xiaobo Chen and colleagues. When AI agents split a request among subagents, handoffs can lose or change requirements. In a preregistered study, researchers compared free-text and structured handoffs with signed manifests that pair quoted requirements with checkable rules. On synthetic tasks, signed manifests cut unsafe decisions under attack from 69.4 percent to 9.0 percent, without reducing compliant decisions compared with structured handoffs. But signatures cannot fix requirements corrupted before signing, making accurate extraction the key point of trust.

arxiv:2611.08180.text: Quantum Advantage with Sign-Free Proofs: An Oracle Separation between StoqMA and MA. From Yassine Hamoudi and colleagues. Classical proof systems can be weaker than quantum ones, but earlier separations often relied on substantial quantum computation. This work shows that even a very limited quantum verifier can outperform every classical verifier relative to an oracle. The verifier uses classical reversible computation followed by a single measurement in the Hadamard basis. The separating task is to estimate a graph's largest eigenvalue, linking this result to the study of sign-free quantum Hamiltonians.

arxiv:2611.07945.text: tok: a textual concrete syntax of BPMN and DMN for humans and AI agents. From Marek Deja. Business process and decision models are often stored in formats that are bulky or difficult for language models to use. Tok offers a plain-text way to describe them, checks models against both standards, and can turn them into XML with diagrams. Across the tested files, tok used fewer tokens and its checker caught more injected errors than existing checks. Language models also produced valid tok models, and a lean tool setup helped them do so with fewer tokens than XML.

arxiv:2611.07360.text: Energy-conserving scheme for a shallow-water model with capillary effects. From Sudarshan Kumar K and colleagues. Capillary effects make shallow-water and thin-film flow models difficult to solve numerically because they involve third-order derivatives. The work rewrites these models using an augmented form with second-order derivatives, then builds a fully discrete scheme that conserves energy. The method applies to both quadratic and fully nonlinear capillary models, including classical shallow-water models. Numerical results show it is stable and preserves total energy when there is no dissipation.

arxiv:2611.07675.text: Randomized Parallel Complexity of Weakly Convex Optimization. From Kang Liu. Finding approximate stationary points of nonsmooth weakly convex functions can require many rounds of queries, even when several queries run at once. In sufficiently high dimensions, the usual subgradient rate is optimal for randomized methods that make polynomially many parallel queries per round. In one dimension, a deterministic search using only function values takes a logarithmic number of rounds, and parallel queries reduce that further. Matching lower bounds show that even access to the full subdifferential at each query cannot beat these limits.
